dataIdInfo.idAbs: This data set contains over 1,000 miles of official recreational trails on land owned and managed by New Jersey State Parks (NJSP). Data collection was a cooperative effort between New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) employees, volunteers, Dovetail Trail Consulting, and non-profit agencies resulting in varying degrees of spatial accuracy and detail. Due to the varied mapping sources this data is not intended for orienteering purposes.

dataIdInfo.idPurp: The purpose is to provide NJSP with a manageable, graphic inventory of trails within the NJSPS system. Besides in-house trail management this data was created for the production of trail maps for hikers, bikers, and horseback riders for safe navigation through official trails in the NJSP. Objective accessibility information was also added for users to determine whether a trail would be user-friendly for them based on their own abilities. These maps are available at https://dep.nj.gov/parksandforests. The data has value to the public, federal, state, county and municipal government agencies, trail organizations and non-profits for local and regional planning decisions for outings, constructing trail connections, land acquisition for trail corridors etc… This data is not intended for orienteering purposes.

Consts.useLimit: This data should not be used for orienteering purposes even though the trails have been reviewed for accuracy. Trails may be altered or closed depending on weather conditions, always check https://www.nj.gov/dep/parksandforests/parks/park_advisories_web.html for the most up to date trail information. prcStep.stepDesc: In 2003 state volunteers, employees, and non-profits began hiking and biking New Jersey’s State Park trails. They collected data by using recreational global positioning systems (GPS) and professional GPS devices. A consistent attribute table and data dictionary developed overtime to best present the collected data. The raw data is then transferred from the GPS device to a shapefile to be georeferenced using 2002/07/12 Imagery (Natural and/or Infrared) and the Statewide_Hillshade layers. As park by park is completed a large aerial image with all data on top is brought to Park employees to verify the accuracy and check for any missing data. In coordination with this feedback changes are made to the shapefile and additional GPSing is done if needed. Once all is finalized the park’s shapefile can be copied to the final trails dataset and the topology tool is conducted to check for overlaps, spurs/overshoots, and intersections.

All newly collected data was gathered with a Trimble Geo7x and georeferenced to 2012 or 2015 orthoimagery. Any preexisting line changes that occurred were referenced from 2015 orthoimagery. The topology tool was conducted to check for overlaps, spurs/overshoots, and intersections.

Added the new RGNL_TRL (Regional Trail) field to state if a trail goes through multiple regions. Also added new data collected with a Trimble Geo7X. This trails layer did not always include regional trails in their entirety. It will be beneficial for users to see this regional trail field to know if a trail continues outside of state lands.

Updated attributes, edited trail features, and added a few trails per superintendent requests. Changes occurred in Allaire, Appalachian Trail, Cape May Point, Double Trouble, Island Beach, Long Pond, Monmouth Battlefield, Norvin Green, Ramapo Mountain, Round Valley, Stokes, Wawayanda, and Worthington. Any trail adjustments were based on 2015 orthoimagery.

Starting in 2025, New Jersey State Parks had Dovetail Trail Consulting assess some of the trails in the central region. They used mobile applications such as Gaia, Avenza, and Sensor Logger to collect data, they provided us with updated trail and new accessibility data in a geodatabase format. The NJ State Park Trail Data was updated to include Dovetail’s accessibility data providing objective information about the trails such as slope, cross slope, and trail width. The collection of accessibility data is incomplete but NJ State Parks will continue to add accessibility information as it is collected.

report.measDesc: The database was thoroughly reviewed for consistency and correctness; it was also maintained throughout production. The data was checked for accuracy in multiple ways. GPS data was reviewed after post-processing on top of one or more of 2002/07/12 Imagery (Natural and/or Infrared) and Statewide_Hillshade layers at 1:500 to 1:1500 scales. Data was then cross-checked by the Park Superintendent and other Park experts. Topology check was conducted for overlaps, spurs/overshoots, and intersections.

The data was checked for accuracy in multiple ways. GPS data was reviewed after post-processing on top of one or more of 2002 or newer Imagery (Natural and/or Infrared) and Statewide_Hillshade layers at 1:500 to 1:1500 scales. Data was then cross-checked by the Park Superintendent and other Park experts. Topology check was conducted for overlaps, spurs/overshoots, and intersections.

Data is available statewide for New Jersey. This dataset is not comprehensive; missing data will be populated on a regular basis. Additionally, new, realigned, or closed trails will require the dataset to be updated on an as needed basis.
